name: Roing
tagline: Idu Mishmi foothills below the snows of Mayudia
meta_description: Roing travel guide: Mayudia pass snow, Mehao Lake, Bhismaknagar ruins, Idu Mishmi culture, real costs and how to reach via the Dhola–Sadiya bridge.
summary: Roing is the headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley, a foothill town at about 390 m where the Idu Mishmi hills meet the Assam plains. It is the base for Mayudia pass, which gets snow in winter, the Mehao Lake hike and the old brick ruins of Bhismaknagar. Stay 2–3 nights between November and March.
intro: Roing lies at the foot of the Mishmi Hills, where rivers from the Dibang valley spread out towards the Brahmaputra. It is a quiet district town of government offices, a market and wide streets, but within an hour you can be in dense forest, at a mountain lake, or climbing towards Mayudia, a pass at about 2,655 m on the road north to Anini that is often white with snow from December to February.

This is the home of the Idu Mishmi, whose shamanic traditions, woven textiles and knowledge of the forest are distinctive. Their main festival, Reh, is held in early February. Adi and other communities also live around Roing, and the plains to the south have a long history: the brick ruins at Bhismaknagar, a short drive away, belong to a fortified town of the medieval Chutiya kingdom.

Getting here became much easier in 2017, when the Dhola–Sadiya bridge across the Lohit opened and cut hours off the road from Tinsukia and Dibrugarh. Roing is low and warm, so the comfortable season runs from October to March. Use it for two or three nights: one day for Mayudia, one for Mehao Lake or the sanctuary, and one for Bhismaknagar and the town.
facts: Oct – Mar; Dec – Feb for snow at Mayudia
Mayudia snow, Mehao Lake, Bhismaknagar ruins, Idu Mishmi culture

highlights.title: Mayudia pass
highlights.text: About 56 km north of Roing on the road to Anini, Mayudia climbs to around 2,655 m and is one of the easiest places in eastern Arunachal to see snow, usually between December and February. Roads can close after heavy falls.

highlights.title: Mehao Lake
highlights.text: A forest lake inside Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary, reached by a steep walk of several hours from near Roing. The trail climbs through evergreen forest; go with a local guide and forest permission, and start early.

highlights.title: Bhismaknagar ruins
highlights.text: About 30 km from Roing, brick walls, gateways and a raised palace complex mark a fortified town of the Chutiya kingdom. The site, excavated by archaeologists, is linked in local tradition with King Bhismaka of the Mahabharata.

highlights.title: Idu Mishmi culture
highlights.text: The Idu Mishmi are known for their igu shamans, finely woven textiles and the Reh festival in early February. A local guide can arrange a respectful village visit and explain customs.

highlights.title: The Dhola–Sadiya bridge
highlights.text: Crossing the Lohit on the way in, this 9.15 km bridge, opened in 2017, is one of the longest in India. On a clear day the Mishmi Hills rise directly ahead.

field_notes.fact: The Dhola–Sadiya Bridge, also called the Bhupen Hazarika Setu, crosses the Lohit river for about 9.15 km. It opened in May 2017 and made Roing a few hours' drive from Tinsukia and Dibrugarh.

Bhismaknagar near Roing is an archaeological site with brick fortifications and a palace complex attributed to the Chutiya kingdom. Local tradition links it with King Bhismaka, father of Rukmini in the Mahabharata.
Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary, which rises directly behind Roing, protects forest from the foothills to high ridges and contains Mehao Lake. It was declared a sanctuary in 1980.

how_to_reach.text: Dibrugarh airport is the usual gateway, about 150 km and 4 hours via Tinsukia and the Dhola–Sadiya bridge. Tezu, further east, has a small airport with limited regional flights; check current status before you travel.
Shared Sumos run from Tinsukia and Dibrugarh to Roing, and buses connect Roing with Pasighat and Tezu. Tinsukia is the nearest major railway station. Buy Sumo seats at the stand early in the morning.

From Tinsukia the road crosses the Dhola–Sadiya bridge and enters Arunachal near the Sadiya side, about 120 km and 3–3.5 hours in all. The Inner Line Permit is checked on entry. From Pasighat allow 4–6 hours, depending on bridges and road works.

where_to_stay: Saver: simple hotels and family homestays in Roing charge about ₹1,500–2,500 a night for a double; ask locally, as the options change. Comfort: a few better hotels and homestays in and around town have attached bathrooms and hot water. Signature: Roing has no luxury hotel. On private trips we use the most comfortable room available and add a local guide and vehicle for Mayudia and Mehao.
tips: For snow at Mayudia, go between December and February and check whether the road is open the evening before.
Start the Mehao Lake walk at first light with a local guide; the descent in fading light is slippery.
Name Lower Dibang Valley on your Inner Line Permit, and Dibang Valley if you go beyond Mayudia to Anini.
Carry warm layers for Mayudia even if Roing feels warm; the pass is over 2,000 m higher.
Ask before photographing igu shamans or rituals during Reh.

experiences.title: A snow day at Mayudia pass
experiences.summary: Drive 56 km up from Roing's warm foothills to Mayudia at about 2,655 m, where snow usually lies from December to February, and come back down the same day.
body: Mayudia sits on the road from Roing to Anini, in the Mishmi Hills. The drive climbs through forest and hairpin bends from under 400 m to about 2,655 m in 2–3 hours, and in winter the change is sudden: a warm morning in Roing, then snow on the trees and the road as you near the top. For many travellers from the plains this is the first snow they touch.

Leave Roing early, as clouds often build by midday. A few simple dhabas and stays operate near the pass in season. Take warm clothing, gloves and shoes with grip; the road can be icy, and after heavy snowfall it may close or need chains. Drivers from Roing know the conditions, so trust their call on how far to go.

Beyond Mayudia the road continues to Anini in Dibang Valley district, which needs that district on your permit and more time. For a day trip, enjoy the pass and return to Roing by late afternoon. Take your rubbish back down. Road status changes daily in winter; check current status before you travel.

faqs.a: Usually between December and February, with the heaviest falls often in January. Snow is never guaranteed on a given day. Ask in Roing the evening before about the road and conditions.

faqs.q: How far is Mayudia from Roing?
faqs.a: About 56 km on the road to Anini, roughly 2–3 hours each way depending on snow and road conditions.

faqs.q: Is the road to Mayudia open in winter?
faqs.a: It is usually open, but heavy snowfall can close it for a time or require chains. Travel with a local driver and check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Forest hike to Mehao Lake
experiences.summary: Climb through evergreen forest inside Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary to a lake in the hills above Roing, with a local guide, an early start and a packed lunch.
body: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary rises steeply behind Roing, and Mehao Lake lies in the forest high above the town. The usual route starts from a trailhead a short drive out of Roing and climbs on a narrow forest path for several hours. It is a demanding day: steep, often muddy, with roots and stream crossings, but the forest is rich and quiet and the lake still and cold.

You need permission from the forest department and a local guide who knows the trail; it is easy to lose the path. Start at first light so that you reach the lake by late morning and are back below the steepest sections well before dark. Carry plenty of water, lunch, a rain jacket and leech socks in damp weather.

Birds are the main wildlife you will notice, though the sanctuary also holds mammals that are rarely seen. Stay on the trail, keep noise low and carry out all rubbish. Conditions vary with weather and trail maintenance, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the Mehao Lake hike?
faqs.a: Most people take a full day for the round trip, with several hours of steep climbing each way. Start at dawn and allow time for rests at the lake.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for Mehao Lake?
faqs.a: Yes. The trail is steep and easy to lose in the forest, and you need forest department permission. A local guide costs about ₹1,500–2,500 for the day.

faqs.q: Is the Mehao Lake trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.a: Only for fit beginners who are comfortable with steep, muddy climbing. Families with young children and anyone unsure on rough ground should consider Bhismaknagar or Mayudia instead.

experiences.title: The brick ruins of Bhismaknagar
experiences.cost: Taxi ₹1,500–2,500 return; entry free or small fee
experiences.summary: Walk the fortifications, gateways and palace mound of a medieval Chutiya town in the forest near Roing, a site that local tradition links with King Bhismaka of the Mahabharata.
body: Bhismaknagar lies in the foothills about 30 km from Roing. Archaeologists have uncovered brick walls, gateways and a large raised complex usually described as a palace, the remains of a fortified town of the Chutiya kingdom that ruled parts of upper Assam in the medieval period. Much of the site is still under forest, so walking it gives a sense of discovery.

In local tradition the site is the capital of King Bhismaka, whose daughter Rukmini married Krishna in the Mahabharata, and the Idu Mishmi have their own stories about Rukmini. Historians link the brickwork to the Chutiya period. Ask a local guide to show you the main walls and gateways and explain both histories.

Go in the morning when it is cooler. Paths can be overgrown and slippery, so wear closed shoes and carry water. There are few facilities at the site. Respect the ruins: do not climb on walls or remove bricks. Combine it with a slow return to Roing for lunch.

faqs.a: Historians attribute the brick fortifications and palace complex to the Chutiya kingdom of medieval upper Assam. Local tradition links the site with King Bhismaka of the Mahabharata.

faqs.q: How far is Bhismaknagar from Roing?
faqs.a: About 30 km, roughly an hour by road. A taxi for the return trip with waiting time costs about ₹1,500–2,500.
Yes, if you enjoy history and quiet sites. It is not grand or restored, but the walls and gateways in the forest are striking, and you will usually have the place almost to yourself.

Fly to Dibrugarh or take a train to Tinsukia, then drive across the Dhola–Sadiya bridge to Roing, about 3–4 hours. Shared Sumos run from Tinsukia and Dibrugarh for about ₹300–500 a seat. Permits are checked on entry to Arunachal.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Roing and Mayudia?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit listing Lower Dibang Valley, and Dibang Valley if you go beyond Mayudia to Anini. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see snow at Mayudia?
faqs.a: December to February, with January often the most reliable. Snow depends on the weather each year. Ask your driver or hotel in Roing the evening before; heavy snow can close the road.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Roing?
faqs.a: October to March, when it is dry and comfortable. December to February adds the chance of snow at Mayudia, and early February brings the Reh festival. April to September is hot and wet, with heavy monsoon rain.

faqs.q: How many days should I spend in Roing?
faqs.a: Two or three nights: one day for Mayudia, one for Mehao Lake or Bhismaknagar, and time in town. Roing pairs well with Namdapha to the south-east and Pasighat to the west.

Reh is the main festival of the Idu Mishmi, held in early February with rituals led by igu shamans, feasting and dances. It is celebrated in Roing and villages of the Dibang valley. Ask before photographing rituals.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs and mobile network in Roing?
faqs.a: Yes. Roing has ATMs and 4G from major networks. Signal fades on the climb to Mayudia and beyond. Carry cash for the day trips.
Yes. The town is calm, Bhismaknagar and the riverbanks are easy outings, and children enjoy the snow at Mayudia. Skip the Mehao Lake hike with young children; it is steep and long.
Yes. Roing is a quiet district town. The main risks are on the roads: ice and snow at Mayudia in winter, landslides in the monsoon and unlit roads at night. Travel with local drivers in winter.
